cohort: 369 pregnant women in Taiwan, including 222 native Taiwanese women and 147 immigrant women
finding: While caesarean delivery rates did not differ between native and immigrant women, maternal complications and household activity support were positively associated with caesarean deliveries, while informational support was a protective factor.
mod_finding: Caesarean rates did not differ significantly between native and immigrant women in Taiwan, regardless of whether the caesarean section was medically indicated or not.
